title: observability(api): propagate request_id & traceparent through API surface; structured logs + per-endpoint metrics tags
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Production incidents and internal debugging showed gaps in correlating API requests across the gateway, runtime, and background workers. Customers and SREs need per-request observability (request_id) and end-to-end trace propagation (W3C traceparent) for troubleshooting, plus consistent structured logs and per-endpoint metric tags to filter dashboards/alerts.

What this PR does (high level):
- Assigns a stable request_id at the edge (API gateway) when absent and propagates it through the request lifecycle via headers and context.
- Ensures W3C traceparent/ tracestate headers are passed through and used by our internal tracer - adds fallback generation when missing.
- Enriches all API-surface logs (gateway, openai-compat layer, routing/marshalling, streaming events) with request_id, trace_id, route (route name), model, and customer_id when present; logs are emitted as structured JSON fields.
- Adds per-endpoint tags to metrics emitted by the runtime and the gateway (route, method, route_version). These tags are used in latency/cost dashboards and SLO-based alerts.
- Stabilizes streaming events by including request_id and event sequence metadata in partial events so downstream consumers can reconcile fragments.
- Tool/function-calling: include call_id (derived from request_id + counter) in function call events and logs for cross-correlating tool invocations.
- OpenAI compatibility: the openai-compat layer now mirrors X-Request-ID / request-id headers to OpenAI-compatible responses and includes request_id/traceparent in the response metadata JSON.
- Adds integration tests and end-to-end CI job that exercises header passthrough, streaming partials with request_id, and a metrics tag smoke test.

Checklist: 
- [x] Generate/propagate request_id at gateway.
- [x] W3C traceparent passthrough and fallback generation.
- [x] Structured JSON logs enriched with request_id and trace_id.
- [x] Per-endpoint metric tags.
- [x] Streaming partials include request_id and seq metadata.
- [x] Tool/function-calling includes call_id.
- [x] OpenAI-compat response metadata enriched.
- [x] Integration tests + CI job.
- [x] Docs and changelog entry.

Testing done: 
- Unit tests for header extraction/setting, JSON log formatting, and call_id generation.
- End-to-end test in perf-canary that simulates 200 concurrent streaming requests and validates all partial events contain request_id.
- Integration test added to the api-integration pipeline that asserts traceparent continuity across gateway->router->runtime and that per-endpoint metrics contain the route tag.
- Manual validation against an internal staging cluster with an observability dashboard (per-endpoint latency) confirming tags are present.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag `obs.request_id_propagation` (default on for hosted).
- Deploy gateway + openai-compat changes first, followed by runtime worker changes.
- Monitor new error-rate and tail-latency SLOs + a dedicated alert that fires if request_id is missing in >1% of 5xx responses.
- Canary rollout to 10% of traffic for 48h, then 50% for 24h, then full rollout.

Notes & limitations:
- When customers already attach their own request-id header, we preserve it. For non-W3C tracers we still try best-effort to map to trace_id.
- Older SDKs that don't surface response metadata may not see the request_id until a client update; gateway also returns X-Request-ID in the HTTP response so customers can correlate.

Files changed (high level):
- gateway/src/http/request_id_middleware.py: new middleware to generate/preserve request_id and traceparent.
- gateway/src/logging/json_logger.py: structured logging helper updated to include request/trace fields.
- openai-compat/src/compat_middleware.py: mirror request_id into response metadata and streaming event envelopes.
- runtime/router/trace_context.py: central helper for trace/request context propagation.
- runtime/streaming/partial_event_emitter.go: include request_id + seq fields on partials.
- runtime/metrics/metrics_tags.go: add route/method tags for metrics emitted from the runtime.
- tests/integration/test_requestid_traceprop.py: E2E tests for header passthrough and streaming partials.
- docs/api-observability.md: documentation of headers and examples.

Summary of commits: 
- 6 commits: init gateway middleware, wire through runtime context, streaming partials + tests, openai-compat mirrors, metrics tagging, docs + changelog.

Why not more invasive changes? We intentionally scoped this to propagation and enrichment to minimize surface area; no protocol changes between internal components, only richer metadata and tags.

Rollback plan: disable feature flag `obs.request_id_propagation` and redeploy gateway, which restores previous behavior immediately.

Related: ENG-8421 (observability baseline), ENG-8450 (streaming stability), SUP-1298 (customer support case requesting request ids for debugging).
commits: feat(runtime): propagate tracecontext and request context
fix(streaming): include request_id in partial event envelopes
feat(openai-compat): expose request_id in response metadata
test: add integration + perf canary tests
docs: add api-observability doc and changelog entry
changed_snippets:
# gateway/src/http/request_id_middleware.py
- if 'X-Request-ID' in req.headers: ctx.request_id = req.headers['X-Request-ID']
+ ctx.request_id = req.headers.get('X-Request-ID') or generate_request_id()
# ensure traceparent passthrough
+ ctx.traceparent = req.headers.get('traceparent') or generate_traceparent()

merge_result: Merged by squash merge on 2026-02-12 by Maya Patel. Commit message: feat(observability): propagate request_id & traceparent through API surface; structured logs + per-endpoint metrics tags. CHANGES: gateway middleware, runtime trace context, streaming partials, openai-compat headers, tests, docs.
release_notes: Added stable request-id propagation and W3C traceparent passthrough across the API surface. Logs are now structured and include request_id and trace_id for easier debugging. Streaming partial events include request_id and sequence metadata. Per-endpoint metric tags (route/method/version) are now emitted for better filtering in dashboards. OpenAI-compat responses include request_id in response metadata. Not a breaking change.
notes_for_ops: Monitor metric: observability.request_id.missing_rate (alert if >1% over 5m). Monitor trace continuity errors (observability.trace.breaks). Canary rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% as documented. Feature flag obs.request_id_propagation controls behavior.
changelog_entry: - Observability: request_id and W3C traceparent propagated across API surface; structured logs enriched; per-endpoint metric tags added; streaming partials include request_id and seq metadata. (2026-02-12)
customer_impact: Customers will see X-Request-ID echoed in responses and can correlate requests across components. No API breaking changes; behavior opt-out via feature flag for private deployments.
security_considerations: Customer-provided request-id is preserved but treated as non-sensitive. We added an allowlist and PII filter before attaching fields like customer_id to logs. No secrets are emitted. Security scan passed.
testing_instructions: Run tests/integration/test_requestid_traceprop.py and perf-canary/scenarios/streaming-requestid.yml. Example curl: curl -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" -H "X-Request-ID: my-client-id-123" https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
